newsitem.title: UK: Alliance faces legal action - paper.
newsitem.headline: Alliance faces legal action - paper.

text.p: British building society Alliance and Leicester faces legal action from dissatisfied members over its planned 2.5 billion stg (US$4.2 billion) stock market flotation, the Times newspaper reported.

The threat of legal action from the Alliance and Leicester Action Group came on Thursday after the building society's board met to discuss a proposed new Building Societies Bill that could affect its plans to float.

The new legislation being drafted at present has abandoned a clause which gives converting societies five years protection from hostile takeover bids. When the Alliance & Leicester drew up its transfer document, which has been mailed to 3.5 million members, it was based on present legislation.

The action group will mount a legal challenge to the conversion plans and will take its case to the Building Societies Commission on the ground that the transfer document is misleading, the Times said.

A spokesman for the action group said the five-year protection for societies was of no benefit to anyone but the directors, the Times reported. "In fact, a predator could enhance the share price for ordinary shareholders," the Times quoted the spokesman as saying.
